summary: A 1956 Ontario fire tower on a hill beside Highway 118 at Haliburton; the cupola has been removed and the frame still stands, per undated sources.

facts.design: Frame tower with a cupola on top; the cupola has since been removed
facts.status_note: The frame still stands with the cupola removed, according to Wikipedia and forestrangers.github.io. Neither source dates that description.

staffing.status: out of use as a fire tower

access.note: The still-standing list says the MNR no longer maintains these towers, has removed the bottom 20 ft of ladder, and asks visitors not to climb. The tower can be seen from Highway 118. No source says whether the hill is open to the public.

facts.agency: Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (built by the former Department of Lands and Forests)

notes_for_editor: The 1956 build, Lindsay district, and late-1960s closure come only from the Dysart et al Wikipedia article, which is undated; there is no second source for the dates. The still-standing list (undated GeoCities copy) and forestrangers.github.io both say the frame still stands, but neither is dated, so current condition is unconfirmed. The list's asterisk key says cupola-removed towers are now used as communications towers; Wikipedia says nothing about radio use, so that claim is single-sourced and the story says so. The firelookout.ca entry has no height, year, type or elevation (all N/A). The Dysart et al municipal fire-history page has no fire tower content. The Muskoka Region Haliburton article in cache has no Dysart-specific text. The Ontario LIO fire-tower layer in data/raw has no feature near these coordinates. No staffing names, fires, or access rule specific to this tower were found. The brief's status 'unknown' is updated to standing per sources. No corrections proposed. The story says 'Dysart et al' and avoids 'county' for this Canadian tower.
